instruction: Tighten this document: cut redundancy, shorten long sentences, and make the prose crisper throughout.
edited_document:
# Sample project review — first stage

<!-- lark:block:l01 -->
## Summary

<!-- lark:block:l02 -->
The reader work dominated stage 1, landed on time, and is now consumed by two consumer projects.

<!-- lark:block:l03 -->
Remaining risk is concentrated in the writer surface: the plan-gated apply engine still refuses several shapes consumers ask for regularly.

<!-- lark:block:l04 -->
## Reliability

<!-- lark:block:l05 -->
Three failed test runs, none in a release, all traced to the same missing field-level permission scope.

<!-- lark:block:l06 -->
The follow-up made failures legible rather than widening any scope — a grant is a console action, not something the library may take.

<!-- lark:block:l07 -->
## Throughput

<!-- lark:block:l08 -->
Cycle time improved once board moves became scripted, eliminating the drift class where folder and log disagreed on an issue's state.

<!-- lark:block:l09 -->
Remaining drag is review latency on larger tranches, where a single reviewer must hold a lot of context at once.

<!-- lark:block:l10 -->
## Consumers

<!-- lark:block:l11 -->
The reference consumer vendors a built wheel and pins a local file requirement, so a release reaches it only when it chooses to refresh.

<!-- lark:block:l12 -->
That has been a good trade: nothing ships by surprise, and the refresh step is where compatibility gets checked.

<!-- lark:block:l13 -->
## Resources

<!-- lark:block:l14 -->
Disk use was flat. The only new space went to the sandbox used for live write gates — small and torn down after each run.

<!-- lark:block:l15 -->
The one avoidable cost was rework from a misdiagnosis that took roughly a week to resolve.

<!-- lark:block:l16 -->
## Second stage

<!-- lark:block:l17 -->
The second stage is planned around round-trip editing — the capability consumers ask for most and cannot currently express.

<!-- lark:block:l18 -->
Everything else is sequenced behind it; a half-built round-trip would be worse than none.

<!-- lark:block:l19 -->
### Risks

<!-- lark:block:l20 -->
- Review latency on large tranches
- A single reviewer holding all the context
- The round-trip work slipping into the following stage

<!-- lark:block:l21 -->
Ordered by likelihood, not by how uncomfortable they are to discuss.

<!-- lark:block:l22 -->
### Numbers

<!-- lark:block:l23 -->
| Metric | Stage 1 | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Failed runs | 3 | 0 |
| Median cycle time | 4.1 days | 3 days |
| Consumer refreshes | 6 | 6 |

<!-- lark:block:l24 -->
Cycle time excludes two issues parked for a maintainer decision; holding time is not review time.

<!-- lark:block:l25 -->
### Decisions needed

<!-- lark:block:l26 -->
Needed: whether the round-trip work ships behind a flag or as the default shape. That decision gates everything after it.
